title: Field deploy mini-log: day notes & gotchas
summary: Quick personal scratchpad from on-site install day: sequence of steps, immediate blockers, short commands and reminders for later handoff.
content:
2026-03-11 08:30 - on site (Customer: FinData Inc)
- Office desk, access badge confirmed (ops contact: @marta).
- Rack A5: 2x T4 nodes, 1x management jumpbox.

Morning walk-through / quick wins
1) Confirmed networking baseline:
   - Customer VPC CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16 (from infra team).
   - Expected subnets: 10.40.1.0/24 (app), 10.40.2.0/24 (db), 10.40.3.0/24 (mgmt).
   - Public egress via NAT gw in us-west-2a -> ensure egress rules allow our outbound TLS to hosted endpoints for agent checks (if using private control-plane, note: offline mode).
2) Jumpbox prep:
   - User: redwood-deployer
   - Ran: sudo yum update -y; sudo systemctl enable --now chronyd
   - Verified time sync: chronyc tracking -> skew < 50ms. Important: KMS cert validation failures when time drift > 1s.
3) GPU node quick check:
   - nvidia-smi shows driver 510.x, CUDA 11.7.
   - Docker runtime used: containerd + nvidia-container-toolkit.
   - Observed one node with high dmesg: "NVML: driver mismatch" -> rebooted that node, driver reloaded, nvidia-smi healthy.

Install sequence (local notes):
- Step A: network baseline + firewall rules
  * Ensure TCP 443 outbound from nodes to api.redwood-hosted.com (unless private control-plane).
  * Open internal port 7777 between app and mgmt subnets for runtime control-plane.
  * MTU: customer had jumbo frames (9000) — force mtu 1500 on container network to avoid packet fragmentation (added note to config: network.mtu=1500).
- Step B: storage mounts
  * Ensure /mnt/model-store mounted before runtime starts. Used NFS v4 on 10.40.2.12:/exports/models.
  * Mount options: rw,noatime,_netdev,vers=4.1 -> fstab entry persisted.
- Step C: secrets & KMS
  * Customer uses AWS KMS via VPC endpoints. Router team must add endpoint for kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com -> request sent (INF-4821).
  * HSM note: if HSM present, confirm PKCS#11 lib path (/usr/local/lib/pkcs11/libhsm.so) and set REDWOOD_KMS_PROVIDER=pkcs11 on jumpbox.
- Step D: agent & runtime
  * Unpack release tarball, export REDWOOD_ENV=onprem; ./install.sh --skip-node-export (we do manual).
  * Systemd unit: redwood-runtime.service with Restart=on-failure, LimitNOFILE=200000.
  * After first start: tail -f /var/log/redwood/runtime.log -> watch for "kernel: unsupported ISA" (indicates incompatible quantized kernels -> fallback to cpu path).

Immediate blockers & debugging notes
- Blocker 1: Customer firewall blocks outbound to hosted model catalog -> agent cannot download model index. Temp workaround: scp model bundle from jumpbox to /mnt/model-store and set local_catalog=true (documented in handoff). Ticket: INF-4823 (assign: samir).
- Blocker 2: SELinux in enforcing mode caused agent to be unable to write /var/lib/redwood/kv -> setsebool -P container_manage_cgroup 1 did not help. Final: added policy module (see linked_artifacts PR).
- Blocker 3: MTU mismatch impacting large token responses (TCP fragmentation) -> reduced container net mtu and enabled TCP MSS clamping on host (iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu).

Quick commands (pasteable)
- systemctl status redwood-runtime.service && journalctl -fu redwood-runtime -n 200\- sudo mount -t nfs 10.40.2.12:/exports/models /mnt/model-store -o rw,noatime,vers=4.1
- iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
- aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --key-id alias/redwood-customer-key --endpoint-url https://kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
- curl -v --resolve api.redwood-hosted.com:443:10.40.3.20 https://api.redwood-hosted.com/healthz

Notes to self / handoff bullets
- Add explicit step in runbook to check system time before KMS operations.
- Provide offline model bundle (sha256 checksums) to customer if catalog fetch blocked.
- Document HSM PKCS11 env var flow and fallback to AWS KMS endpoint.
- Add a short troubleshooting checklist for SELinux policy failures (audit2allow capture + module build).

Parking lot / follow-ups
- Confirm with network team whether we can request VPC endpoint for KMS (INF-4821).
- Verify long-run kernel module stability on the node with previous NVML warning (watch for regression over next 72h).
- Prepare sanitized handoff doc (1 page) for customer ops: include commands above + environment variables + expected service endpoints.

Open Jira refs: INF-4821 (kms endpoint), INF-4823 (model-catalog firewall), INF-4830 (selinux policy module).

Signed: Evan M. (personal scratchpad)

-- end of day mini-log --

Random brain-dump:
- Consider adding an installer flag --force-local-catalog that copies model bundle from installer tarball to /mnt/model-store and skips network catalog check (useful for airgapped installs).
- Check if containerd version supports cgroup v2; metrics exporter misreports when cgroup v1 assumptions present.
- When running on-prem private control-plane, include a lightweight healthcheck proxy on jumpbox to reduce outbound TLS count from nodes.
